title: Reperfusion Strategies in Donation After Circulatory Death Heart Transplantation: An Up-to-Date Narrative Review
one_line_summary: This narrative review synthesizes global clinical protocols, technical parameters, ethical issues, and recipient outcomes across direct procurement, normothermic regional perfusion, and hypothermic machine perfusion strategies in controlled donation after circulatory death heart transplantation.
key_pearls: - **Donation after circulatory death (DCD)** heart transplantation expands the adult donor heart pool by **15–30%** and reduces waitlist **mortality** by **40%**.

- **Functional warm ischemic time (fWIT)**, measured from systolic blood pressure **< 50 mmHg** or **SpO2 < 75%** to reperfusion/cardioplegia, must remain **< 30 min** (up to **45 min** under extended observation laws).

- **Direct procurement and perfusion (DPP)** using **ex situ** normothermic machine perfusion (**Organ Care System / OCS**) yields an **89%** organ utilization rate and 1-year recipient **survival** of **93.3%**.

- **Thoraco-abdominal normothermic regional perfusion (TA-NRP)** provides **in situ** cardiac assessment (**CI > 2.2–2.5 L/min/m2**, **CVP < 12 mmHg**, **PCWP < 12 mmHg**) and reduces **severe primary graft dysfunction (PGD)** by **60%** compared to DPP.

- **Direct procurement and hypothermic oxygenated perfusion (DP-HOPE)** at **8 °C** reduces myocardial metabolic demand in a non-beating state, achieving **100%** early **survival** without requiring complex normothermic logistics.

- Novel techniques like **Rapid Recovery with Extended Ultraoxygenated Preservation (REUP)** and **beating heart transplantation** minimize dual-arrest ischemia-reperfusion injury, demonstrating **96%** 30-day **survival**.
population: Controlled donation after circulatory death (cDCD) heart donors and adult or pediatric heart transplant recipients

sections.heading: Introduction and Historical Background
sections.content:
- Heart transplantation represents the gold standard for end-stage heart failure, but waitlist **mortality** remains at **7%** due to severe donor organ shortages.
- Implementation of **controlled donation after circulatory death (cDCD)** programs expands adult heart transplant volume by **15–30%**, decreases waitlist **mortality** by **40%**, and reduces overall time on waitlists.
- The first human-to-human heart transplant by Dr. Christian Barnard in **1967** utilized a circulatory death donor following a **5-minute** observation period.
- Historical adoption of **donation after brain death (DBD)** predominated after the **1968** Harvard criteria and the **1981** US Uniform Determination of Death Act.
section_pearls: cDCD programs increase heart transplant volume by 15-30% and reduce waitlist mortality by 40%.
The first human heart transplant in 1967 utilized a circulatory death donor.

sections.heading: DCD Definitions and Warm Ischemia Dynamics
sections.content:
- **Maastricht Category III** donors (withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy / *WLST*) represent the main donor pool for cDCD heart transplantation.
- Agonal phase inadequate organ perfusion is strictly defined as systolic arterial pressure **< 50 mmHg** and/or **SpO2 < 75%**.
- Mandated post-asystole **no-touch periods** vary globally from **2 to 30 min** (**5 min** standard in most countries; **20 min** of electrical silence required in Italy).
- **Functional warm ischemic time (fWIT)** spans from inadequate organ perfusion to reperfusion or cardioplegia administration and should ideally remain **< 30 min** (tolerated up to **45 min** under longer legal no-touch rules).
- Myocardial biomyocyte studies confirm exponential drops in contractility, loss of mitochondrial function, and elevated cell apoptosis beyond **10 min** of cardiac arrest.
section_pearls: Inadequate perfusion onset is defined as SBP < 50 mmHg or SpO2 < 75%.
fWIT should be kept < 30 min, though up to 45 min is tolerated in long no-touch protocols.

sections.heading: Direct Procurement Strategies: DP-CS, DPP, and DP-HOPE
sections.content:
- **Direct Procurement and Cold Storage (DP-CS)** relies on immediate post-mortem cardiectomy and static cooling, requiring donor-recipient co-localization without objective functional evaluation.
- **Direct Procurement and Perfusion (DPP)** uses *ex situ* normothermic machine perfusion (**Organ Care System / OCS**) with warm blood at **34 °C**, targeting coronary flow **650–900 mL/min**, mean aortic pressure **65–90 mmHg**, and perfusate lactate **< 5 mmol/L**.
- Randomized US clinical trial evaluating **DPP** demonstrated an **89%** heart utilization rate, **93.3%** 1-year **survival**, and **20%** rate of moderate-to-severe *PGD*.
- **Direct Procurement and Hypothermic Oxygenated Perfusion (DP-HOPE)** continuously perfuses an oxygenated cardioplegic solution with RBCs (**hematocrit 10–15%**) at **8 °C** under a root pressure of **20 mmHg** (**150–250 mL/min** flow).
- Early clinical series of **DP-HOPE** in adult and pediatric heart transplantation showed **100%** 30-day **survival** with no severe *PGD*.
section_pearls: DPP using the OCS device targets coronary flow of 650-900 mL/min and lactate < 5 mmol/L.
DP-HOPE maintains non-beating preservation at 8 °C with hyperoncotic oxygenated perfusate.

sections.heading: Normothermic Regional Perfusion (TA-NRP) and Ethical Considerations
sections.content:
- **Thoraco-abdominal Normothermic Regional Perfusion (TA-NRP)** establishes *in situ* normothermic oxygenated circulation via **ECMO** or **CPB** after clamping and venting supra-aortic trunks, targeting blood flow **> 5 L/min**, **MAP 70–90 mmHg**, and temperature **> 35 °C**.
- Graft acceptance parameters following **TA-NRP** weaning include **Cardiac Index (CI) > 2.2–2.5 L/min/m2**, **CVP < 12 mmHg**, **PCWP < 12 mmHg**, and **LVEF > 50%**.
- Combining **TA-NRP** with static cold storage (**NRP-CS**) substantially lowers equipment costs while matching DBD outcomes (**88.8–90%** 1-year **survival**).
- Cerebral reperfusion concerns are mitigated by surgical ligation, clamping, and open atmospheric venting or transection of brachiocephalic arteries, maintaining zero intracranial perfusion.
- Premortem interventions (such as **heparin** administration or arterial cannulation) are ethically governed and vary by country.
section_pearls: TA-NRP requires clamping and venting supra-aortic trunks to guarantee zero cerebral perfusion.
NRP weaning parameters require CI > 2.2-2.5 L/min/m2, LVEF > 50%, and PCWP < 12 mmHg.

sections.heading: Comparative Outcomes, Organ Yield, and Cost Dynamics
sections.content:
- An international study of **504 cDCD** heart transplants demonstrated that **TA-NRP** achieved a **60%** reduction in severe *PGD* and a **40%** reduction in treated acute cellular rejection compared to **DPP**.
- Extended *ex situ* machine perfusion duration exceeding **8 hours** during **DPP** correlates with decreased long-term recipient **survival**.
- **TA-NRP** improves concurrent liver graft utilization and decreases delayed graft function in abdominal organs without compromising lung procurement or recipient outcomes.
- Organ acquisition costs for **DCD** heart transplantation average **57%** higher than **DBD**, driven by **43%** higher preservation technology costs and **64%** higher transportation fees.
section_pearls: TA-NRP reduces severe PGD by 60% compared to DPP.
Ex situ normothermic machine perfusion > 8 hours is associated with worse recipient survival.

sections.heading: Emerging Techniques: REUP and Beating Heart Implantation
sections.content:
- **Rapid Recovery with Extended Ultraoxygenated Preservation (REUP)** involves an immediate post-mortem sternotomy and controlled **4 °C** hyperoxygenated flush (100% FiO2) at **80 mmHg** root pressure for **10–12 min**, bypassing *in situ* regional perfusion and complex NMP machines.
- Initial clinical series of **24 REUP** heart transplants demonstrated **96%** 30-day **survival** and a low **4%** rate of severe *PGD*.
- **Beating heart transplantation** maintains continuous warm oxygenated coronary blood perfusion via tandem OCS and CPB during donor cardiectomy and recipient implantation.
- Continuous warm beating perfusion eliminates dual rounds of cold static arrest and warm ischemia-reperfusion injury (*IRI*), yielding **100%** early **survival** in preliminary cohorts.
section_pearls: REUP provides rapid cold ultraoxygenated flush without requiring TA-NRP or ex situ normothermic devices.
Beating heart transplantation maintains continuous coronary flow to eliminate cold ischemic arrest.

strengths_limitations:
- **Strengths**: Comprehensive global review of technical protocols, hemodynamic metrics, legal frameworks, and comparative clinical outcomes across all cDCD heart preservation modalities.
- **Limitations**: Absence of randomized controlled trials comparing TA-NRP, DPP, and DP-HOPE directly; heavy reliance on retrospective registries and single-center observational series; potential organ selection bias across international jurisdictions.

drugs_doses.dose: 300 UI/kg or 30,000 UI IV single bolus
drugs_doses.indication: Systemic anticoagulation prior to WLST or immediately following declaration of death during DCD organ procurement
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Bleeding, ethical restrictions regarding ante-mortem administration in specific legal jurisdictions

drugs_doses.dose: 1 L cold crystalloid solution delivered into the aortic root
drugs_doses.indication: Rapid myocardial electromechanical arrest and hypothermic protection during direct heart procurement
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Coronary endothelial shear stress or ischemic injury if post-procurement preservation is prolonged

drugs_doses.dose: Continuous micro-infusion in maintenance perfusate (0–30 mL/h)
drugs_doses.indication: Coronary vasodilation and coronary flow optimization during ex situ normothermic machine perfusion (OCS)
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: AV block, severe bradycardia, excessive systemic coronary vasodilation

drugs_doses.dose: Titrated continuous infusion during ex situ perfusion
drugs_doses.indication: Hemodynamic control to maintain aortic pressure (65–90 mmHg) and heart rate (65–100 bpm) on OCS circuit
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Tachycardia, excessive myocardial oxygen demand, ventricular arrhythmias

drugs_doses.dose: Continuous infusion titrated up to maximum 5 mcg/kg/min
drugs_doses.indication: Inotropic support during donor cardiac functional assessment while weaning from CPB during TA-NRP
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Tachyarrhythmias, increased myocardial ischemia, peripheral vasodilation

drugs_doses.dose: 2 L cold ultraoxygenated solution administered over 10–12 min at 80 mmHg root pressure
drugs_doses.indication: Myocardial arrest and ultraoxygenated protection in the Rapid Recovery with Extended Ultraoxygenated Preservation (REUP) protocol

drugs_doses.dose: Additive to REUP extracorporeal flush circuit prime
drugs_doses.indication: Donor endocrine resuscitation and metabolic reconditioning during REUP hyperoxygenated preservation
